meta.title: Who wrote "You've Got a Friend"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: James Taylor had the No. 1 hit — but Carole King wrote "You've Got a Friend", and recorded it herself on Tapestry the same year. Who wrote it, and whose version is the one everyone knows.
meta.ogDescription: Carole King wrote it and recorded it first, on Tapestry. James Taylor's 1971 single was the hit — and the version most people picture.

writing.label: Written by Carole King — James Taylor had the hit single
writing.sourceLine: James Taylor’s recording went to No. 1 and won him a Grammy, and for most listeners it simply is ‘You’ve Got a Friend’. But he didn’t write it, and he wasn’t the first to record it: Carole King wrote every word and note, and released her own version on Tapestry the same year.
writing.definitiveVersion: James Taylor’s 1971 single — his only US No. 1, and the Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Performance, Male.
trail: The song is credited solely to Carole King on both recordings and in its 1972 Grammy win for Song of the Year — an award that goes to the writer, not the performer.

King recorded it herself for Tapestry, released in February 1971. James Taylor cut his version around the same time — with King playing piano on it — and released it as a single that April; it reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 that summer.

Taylor won the Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Performance (Male) for the recording; King won Song of the Year for the writing. The two awards, to two different people for the same song, are the cleanest record of who did what.

context.heading: Why the singer gets the credit
lead: This is not a case of anyone being wrongly credited — James Taylor really did record ‘You’ve Got a Friend’, and it’s one of his signature performances. What gets lost is that the song is Carole King’s, top to bottom.

It’s an easy thing to lose. A hit single puts a face and a voice to a song, and that pairing is what sticks; the person who wrote the words at a piano months earlier rarely does. King and Taylor were close collaborators — she played on his record, he sang on hers — which makes the split especially easy to blur.
context.pull: Two Grammys, one song: Taylor for singing it, King for writing it.

authors.name: Carole King
authors.bio: One of the most successful songwriters of the 20th century, first with Gerry Goffin in the Brill Building era and then on her own. Tapestry (1971), which includes her own recording of ‘You’ve Got a Friend’, was one of the best-selling albums of its decade.

authors.name: James Taylor
authors.bio: His 1971 single of ‘You’ve Got a Friend’ became his only US No. 1 and won the Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Performance, Male. He wrote much of his own catalogue — but not this one.

schema.faqAnswer: "You've Got a Friend" was written by Carole King, who also recorded it on her 1971 album Tapestry. James Taylor's 1971 single is the version most people know; it reached No. 1 and won him a Grammy, but he did not write the song.
